do: Ensure focus moves in a logical, meaningful order that follows the visual layout
Use HTML source order to control focus sequence rather than scripting
Use positive tabindex values only for custom widgets; default tabindex=0 for natural flow
Keep DOM order and visual order in sync to avoid confusion
Implement keyboard navigation order consistent with reading order
Ensure modals trap focus within and return focus to the triggering element when closed
Manage focus when dynamically adding or removing content (e.g., SPA route changes)
Use focus management APIs (element.focus()) sparingly and predictably
Ensure hidden content (display:none) is removed from focus order
Ensure focusable controls in carousels and tabs follow visual progression
Test focus order with screen readers to verify NVDA/JAWS read sequence
Confirm focus order between grouped form controls follows logical grouping
Ensure skip-to navigation links receive focus before main content
Use tabindex='-1' to send focus to non-focusable elements when needed (e.g., heading after skip link)
Maintain a consistent focus order across screen sizes and responsive layouts
Set focus programmatically only when it improves user context (e.g., after form submission or error)
Test focus behavior in both forward (Tab) and reverse (Shift+Tab) directions
Use meaningful tab order when custom widgets are implemented (e.g., listboxes, date pickers)
Temporarily remove elements from focus order when they are disabled or hidden using tabindex='-1'
Use scripting (e.g., .focus()) to manage focus transitions in single-page applications (SPAs)
Align focus sequence with aria-flowto when deviating source order
Maintain focus order when content is reordered via JavaScript
Ensure focus order on responsive layouts (desktop vs mobile) remains logical
Test focus order in both light and dark modes
Document custom focus order patterns in design system guidelines
dont: Do not rely on tabindex > 0 to reorder focus (F56 failure)
Do not skip interactive elements in focus order
Do not create keyboard traps where focus cannot move forward/backward
Do not manage focus unpredictably on each interaction
Do not rely on visual cues alone; focus must follow semantic structure
Do not mix DOM order and CSS positioning to change focus sequence
Do not use focus() in event handlers that interfere with natural order
Do not allow focus to jump unexpectedly or out of visual/logical order
Do not trap keyboard focus in non-modal containers
Do not hide elements from sighted users while still keeping them in the focus order
Do not allow background content to receive focus when modal dialogs are active
Do not use display: none or visibility: hidden on elements that are currently focused
Do not place off-screen or invisible elements in the tab order unless intentionally needed
Do not use JavaScript to move focus between unrelated elements during keyboard navigation
Do not override expected keyboard behavior (e.g., prevent Tab from advancing focus)
edge_cases: Modal dialogs: Trap focus while open, restore on close
Drawer/side panels: Manage focus when opened/closed
Tabs: Focus moves to tablist then into panel content
Accordions: Focus remains on header after collapse/expand
Carousels: Arrow keys navigate items; Tab moves out
Infinite scroll: Insert items without disrupting focus order
Dynamic forms: Add/remove inputs without losing user focus
Skip links: Visible and functional as first focusable element
SVG with interactive elements: Ensure graphical elements in focus order
Canvas controls: Provide fallback controls in DOM
Live regions: Don’t auto-focus on updates unless necessary
Rich text editors: Manage focus between toolbar and editing area
Forms with grouped controls: Sequential focus by group then item
Context menus: Focus moves into menu and returns
Keyboard shortcuts: Don’t override default Tab focus sequence
Nested modals: Manage focus in stack order
Role=”application” regions: Explicit focus management required
Offscreen content: Ensure removed from focus order
Disabled elements: Should be skipped in Tab sequence
Single-page applications (SPAs): On route change, set focus to the new page title or main heading
In-page navigation (e.g., anchor links): Programmatically set focus to the target heading or landmark
Auto-focused search inputs: Only set focus if it doesn't disrupt user task flow
Hidden tabs or panels: Remove from tab order until they become active
Focusable SVG elements: Ensure tab order is meaningful when SVGs contain links or buttons
RTL (right-to-left) languages: Verify focus order follows reading direction
Floating action buttons (FABs): Place logically in DOM, even if visually positioned at bottom right
Focus moves in a different sequence than the visual presentation.
Dynamically added or removed elements shift tab order unexpectedly.
Focus skips important elements or moves to hidden content.
Overuse of tabindex changes the expected navigation logic.
Automated scanning can confirm focusable elements but not logical flow of movement.
Focus management in single-page applications during content updates.
Complex widgets focus patterns that don't follow standard tab sequences.
